source.name: sp_GetInventorySnapshot
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_GetInventorySnapshot
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    -- Uses NOLOCK hint (dirty reads for performance)
    SELECT
        p.ProductID,
        p.ProductName,
        p.StockQuantity,
        p.Price
    FROM dbo.Products p WITH (NOLOCK)
    WHERE p.StockQuantity > 0
    ORDER BY p.StockQuantity ASC;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_GetInventorySnapshot()
RETURNS TABLE (
    ProductID INTEGER,
    ProductName TEXT,
    StockQuantity INTEGER,
    Price NUMERIC
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- PostgreSQL uses MVCC; no equivalent to NOLOCK needed
    -- Returns result set directly
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        p.ProductID,
        p.ProductName,
        p.StockQuantity,
        p.Price
    FROM dbo.Products p
    WHERE p.StockQuantity > 0
    ORDER BY p.StockQuantity ASC;
END;
$$;
assumptions: ProductID is mapped to INTEGER (assuming SQL Server INT type)
ProductName is mapped to TEXT (assuming SQL Server VARCHAR/NVARCHAR type)
StockQuantity is mapped to INTEGER (assuming SQL Server INT type)
Price is mapped to NUMERIC (assuming SQL Server DECIMAL/NUMERIC/MONEY type)
The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL or will be created
The Products table structure matches the assumed column types
SET NOCOUNT ON is not needed in PostgreSQL functions (no row count messages by default)
NOLOCK hint removed as PostgreSQL uses MVCC for concurrency control

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's NOLOCK hint allows dirty reads (READ UNCOMMITTED). PostgreSQL uses MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) and does not support dirty reads. The default READ COMMITTED isolation level in PostgreSQL provides consistent snapshots without blocking, which is generally safer than NOLOCK while still providing good performance.

Converted from PROCEDURE to FUNCTION returning TABLE because the original procedure returns a result set. Call syntax changes from 'EXEC sp_GetInventorySnapshot' to 'SELECT * FROM sp_GetInventorySnapshot()'
PostgreSQL functions do not send row count messages by default, so SET NOCOUNT ON is unnecessary and has been removed
PostgreSQL treats unquoted identifiers as case-insensitive (folded to lowercase). If 'dbo' schema doesn't exist, consider using 'public' schema or creating the 'dbo' schema explicitly
